label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
**WRITTEN STATEMENT – STUDENT RETURNED TO SCHOOL**

**To:** Mrs. Okafor
**Copy to:** Darlene [Last Name], Transportation Supervisor, and driver file
**From:** [Your Full Name], Driver, Bus 41
**Date:** [Date you turn it in]
**Re:** Complaint dated October 29, regarding the afternoon run on Tuesday, October 27

Mrs. Okafor,

My supervisor gave me a copy of your complaint on November 3 and asked me to put my account of that afternoon in writing. I understand this statement goes in my file and a copy goes to you, so I am writing it to you directly. I want to be respectful about this. I still drive Amara every day and I want things to be right between us.

**What happened**

On Tuesday, October 27, I was driving the afternoon elementary run on Route 9, Bus 41. Amara's stop is Kessler Avenue and Brandt Street. Amara has the green tag on her backpack. For our drivers that tag means an adult has to be at the stop to meet her before I can let her off.

The schedule has me at that stop at 3:50. I got there at 3:52. I stopped, looked for an adult at the corner, and waited until about 3:55. I did not see anyone at the corner or anyone I could tell was there for Amara.

The district rule for kindergarten riders is that if no adult is at the stop, the student stays on the bus and goes back to the school, and the school contacts the parent. I followed that rule. At 3:56 I radioed dispatch. Gloria at dispatch called the school to let them know Amara was coming back.

I still had three more stops and 14 students on the bus, so I finished the route. I got Amara back to Fairmont Elementary at 4:31 and walked her into the office myself. I handed her to Mrs. Petrakis.

**How Amara was doing**

Amara was fine the whole time. She sat in her seat and colored on her folder. At one point she asked if she could ride some more. I told her we were going on a little extra trip today. I kept it light because I did not want her scared. She was not upset when I walked her in.

**About not seeing you**

I understand you were parked across Brandt Street by the laundromat and waved to me. I want to be honest that I did not see you. A box truck was parked on that side of the street, and from my seat I could not see past it. I was not ignoring you. If I had seen you I would have waited for you.

I also want to explain why I didn't get off and look across the street. I had 14 children on the bus. I cannot leave them alone on a running bus to cross the road and search for a parent. That is not safe and it is not something I am allowed to do.

**About the comment that I "drove off laughing"**

I was not laughing. As I pulled away from the stop, a fourth grader in seat 2 was standing up, and I was telling him to sit back down. I understand that from across the street it might have looked like I was talking or smiling, but nothing about that afternoon was funny to me, and I would never laugh at a parent who was worried about her child.

**Request for camera footage**

I am asking the transportation office to pull the camera footage from Bus 41 for the afternoon of October 27. The camera will show the stop at Kessler and Brandt, how long I waited, what could be seen from the bus, and what was happening inside the bus when I pulled away. I think the footage will help everyone, including you, Mrs. Okafor, see what I saw.

**How I feel about this**

I want you to know I understand how frightening that must have been. I have grandchildren, and if I watched a bus pull away with one of them on it, I would have been scared too. I am sorry you had such a bad afternoon. I mean that.

I cannot apologize for following the rule, though. The rule is there to keep the youngest children from being let off with no adult there to take them. If I could not see an adult, I had to treat it as no adult being there. I would make the same call again for any kindergartner on my bus, because I could never live with letting a little one off at a corner by herself.

This has happened once before on my route, years back, with a different family. They were upset at the time too, but afterward they thanked me for keeping their child safe. I hope in time you will see that I was trying to look out for Amara.

**A request going forward**

So this does not happen again, I would ask that whoever picks Amara up wait on the same side of the street as the bus, at the corner, or step out of the car where I can see them clearly. Cars and trucks park along Brandt, and from the driver's seat it is hard to see across to the other side. If I can see you, I will let Amara off right away. If you are running late or something changes, calling the school or the transportation office ahead of time helps too.

**For the record**

I have been driving for 28 years with no write-ups. I take the job seriously, and the safety of the children on my bus comes first. On October 27 I did what the district policy says to do for a kindergarten rider with no adult at the stop.

Mrs. Okafor, I am glad to keep driving Amara. She is a sweet girl and she is no trouble at all. I want this fixed between us, and if you would ever like to talk with me and Darlene together, I am willing to do that.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[Your Full Name]
Driver, Bus 41, Route 9
[Employee ID, if required]
[Date]

---

A few notes before you turn it in:

- Fill in your name, Darlene's last name, your employee number if they use one, and the date. It's due by Friday, November 13.
- Keep a copy for yourself.
- When you give it to Darlene, ask her out loud to put in the request for the Bus 41 footage from October 27 so it gets saved. Some systems record over old footage after a while, and it's already been a couple of weeks.
- Read it over once. If anything isn't exactly how it happened, change it. It's going in your record, so every detail needs to be right.
